## {.nostretch}

```{=html}
<div style="width:100%;height:720px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:26px 48px 30px 48px;background:#ffffff;color:#1f2937;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;display:flex;flex-direction:column;text-align:left;">
  <div style="border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;padding-bottom:8px;margin-bottom:16px;">
    <h1 style="font-size:28px;line-height:1.12;font-weight:720;color:#1f2a44;letter-spacing:-0.1px;margin:0;padding:0;white-space:nowrap;">Model Fitting: Training Design and Fair Comparison</h1>
  </div>

  <p style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.35;color:#344054;margin:0 0 20px 0;padding:0;max-width:1120px;">The fitting process was designed to keep the model comparison fair: the same processed data, split logic, and primary metric were used across all models.</p>

  <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr;gap:20px;align-items:stretch;margin-top:4px;">
    <div style="border-top:3px solid #315f9f;padding:18px 8px 0 8px;min-height:360px;box-sizing:border-box;">
      <div style="font-size:23px;font-weight:760;color:#315f9f;margin-bottom:20px;">Training design</div>
      <div style="display:grid;gap:18px;">
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">80/20 stratified split</strong> kept class proportions similar in training and test sets.</div>
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">3-fold cross-validation</strong> was used within the training set during fitting.</div>
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">Fixed random seed</strong> made the results reproducible.</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div style="border-top:3px solid #315f9f;padding:18px 8px 0 8px;min-height:360px;box-sizing:border-box;">
      <div style="font-size:23px;font-weight:760;color:#315f9f;margin-bottom:20px;">Fair comparison</div>
      <div style="display:grid;gap:18px;">
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">Same feature matrix</strong> was used for all candidate models.</div>
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">Test data was excluded</strong> during fitting and tuning.</div>
        <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;"><strong style="color:#1f2a44;">Macro F1-score</strong> was the primary metric because each satisfaction class should matter equally.</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div style="border-top:3px solid #315f9f;padding:18px 8px 0 8px;min-height:360px;box-sizing:border-box;">
      <div style="font-size:23px;font-weight:760;color:#315f9f;margin-bottom:20px;">5-class → 3-class logic</div>
      <p style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.34;color:#344054;margin:0 0 18px 0;padding:0;">The 3-class experiment used the same preprocessing design, with only the target labels remapped.</p>
      <table style="width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:20px;color:#1f2a44;font-weight:720;">
        <tr><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-top:1px solid #d7dee8;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;">JobSat 0–3</td><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-top:1px solid #d7dee8;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;text-align:right;color:#315f9f;">Dissatisfied</td></tr>
        <tr><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;">JobSat 4–6</td><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;text-align:right;color:#315f9f;">Neutral</td></tr>
        <tr><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;">JobSat 7–10</td><td style="padding:12px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;text-align:right;color:#315f9f;">Satisfied</td></tr>
      </table>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div style="margin-top:auto;font-size:22px;line-height:1.3;color:#1f2a44;background:#f8fbff;border:1px solid #d6e4fb;padding:13px 18px;border-radius:12px;text-align:center;font-weight:720;box-sizing:border-box;">Overall, all models were fitted under the same split, features, and primary metric to support a fair comparison.</div>
</div>
```

## {.nostretch}

```{=html}
<div style="width:100%;height:720px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:26px 48px 30px 48px;background:#ffffff;color:#1f2937;font-family:Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;display:flex;flex-direction:column;text-align:left;">
  <div style="border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;padding-bottom:8px;margin-bottom:16px;">
    <h1 style="font-size:28px;line-height:1.12;font-weight:720;color:#1f2a44;letter-spacing:-0.1px;margin:0;padding:0;white-space:nowrap;">Selected Models and Why We Used Them</h1>
  </div>

  <p style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.35;color:#344054;margin:0 0 18px 0;padding:0;max-width:1120px;">The model set was chosen to compare simple baselines with more flexible methods, while keeping the explanation clear for a multi-class satisfaction task.</p>

  <div style="display:grid;gap:0;border-top:1px solid #d7dee8;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;margin-top:4px;">
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:330px 1fr;gap:26px;padding:19px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;align-items:start;">
      <div style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.18;font-weight:760;color:#1f2a44;">Multinomial Logistic Regression</div>
      <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.32;color:#344054;">A simple linear baseline, used to check whether satisfaction can be predicted from additive effects of the features.</div>
    </div>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:330px 1fr;gap:26px;padding:19px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;align-items:start;">
      <div style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.18;font-weight:760;color:#1f2a44;">Decision Tree</div>
      <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.32;color:#344054;">A rule-based model, used because its decision paths are easy to explain and can reveal simple split patterns.</div>
    </div>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:330px 1fr;gap:26px;padding:19px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;align-items:start;">
      <div style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.18;font-weight:760;color:#1f2a44;">Gradient Boosting</div>
      <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.32;color:#344054;">A boosted tree model, used because it can capture feature interactions and usually works well with structured survey data.</div>
    </div>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:330px 1fr;gap:26px;padding:19px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dee8;align-items:start;">
      <div style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.18;font-weight:760;color:#1f2a44;">Naive Bayes</div>
      <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.32;color:#344054;">A simple probabilistic benchmark, used to test whether a fast model can provide a useful comparison point.</div>
    </div>
    <div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:330px 1fr;gap:26px;padding:19px 0;align-items:start;">
      <div style="font-size:22px;line-height:1.18;font-weight:760;color:#1f2a44;">Fully Connected Neural Network</div>
      <div style="font-size:20px;line-height:1.32;color:#344054;">A non-linear model, used to test whether more flexible learning improves prediction beyond traditional models.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div style="margin-top:auto;font-size:22px;line-height:1.3;color:#1f2a44;background:#f8fbff;border:1px solid #d6e4fb;padding:13px 18px;border-radius:12px;text-align:center;font-weight:720;box-sizing:border-box;">Together, these models cover linear, rule-based, boosted, probabilistic, and neural approaches under the same fitting design.</div>
</div>
```
